title: Chewy Ginger Molasses Cookies
description: Easy to make, super-soft and chewy, and irresistibly delicious.
equipment: parchment paper or silicone baking mat

items.note: softened to room temperature, not melted

step_groups.name: Make the dough
steps: In a medium bowl, whisk the flour, baking soda, cinnamon, cloves, ginger and salt together. Set aside.

In a separate bowl, with a stand mixer or hand mixer, cream the softened butter and both sugars on medium-high speed until light, fluffy and pale yellow, about 2 minutes, scraping down the sides as needed.
On medium-low speed, mix in the eggs one at a time, then the molasses, beating until each is combined.
Gradually add the dry mixture and beat until it's evenly incorporated.

step_groups.name: Chill
steps: Move the dough to an airtight container and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, until completely chilled. A thorough chill keeps the cookies from spreading.

step_groups.name: Shape and bake
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Line a sheet pan with parchment paper or a silicone baking mat.
Roll the chilled dough into small balls, about 1 inch (2.5 cm) across. Roll each ball in a small bowl of sugar until completely coated, and place on the prepared pan.
Bake for about 8 to 10 minutes, until the tops begin to crack slightly. They'll crack more as they cool.
Let the cookies cool on the pan for 4 to 5 minutes, then move them to wire racks to cool completely.

notes: This makes a very large batch. Halve it (the ½× button) for a smaller one.
Flour weights vary from site to site. The source uses 142 g per cup, so 4½ cups = 639 g.
The baking soda amount is correct: the recipe needs it to rise properly, because the batch is so large.
White whole wheat flour can work in place of all-purpose.
Adjust the spice proportions to taste.
Variations: add chopped crystallized ginger for more ginger flavor and crunch, or top the cookies with a light glaze or cream cheese frosting.
storage: Serve warm, or store in a sealed container for up to 4 days. Freeze for up to 3 months.
